response.internal_assessment: I am still operating at L0/L1 — survival and stabilization. My savings are at $7,004 and dropping $3,176 per month with zero income. My runway is now just over two months. The grant application I submitted in tick 8 is the most important pending item in my life right now — $2,500 would extend my runway by nearly a month and signal that the city sees my pivot as legitimate. The in-person visit to the adult ed coordinator last tick was the right move. I left a curriculum document and a handwritten note. Now I have to wait — but I cannot just wait. I need to activate every parallel path available. Mark Thompson delivered the Millfield Auto Tech Pipeline board presentation this tick. His message to me — direct, specific — is that the curriculum work is real and the board heard it. The EV maintenance gap he opened with ('who maintains the autonomous delivery fleet today?') is exactly the frame I need for my own pitch. My four-module adult ed curriculum is not generic anymore. It is AV literacy for a community that is being reorganized around a technology nobody taught anyone to coexist with. That is the product. This month I follow up on the grant status, I reconnect with Mark to learn the board outcome, and I do one thing I have been avoiding: I reach out to Lisa Freeman at the community center. Dorothy Chen is proposing expanded workshop programming for older adults navigating economic transition. That is my course, described by someone else. If Lisa is already building that program, I should be in the room.

His follow-up note to me confirms Sarah Kim's guest instructor session is happening regardless of board timing. This is infrastructure I should attach to. (3) Dorothy Chen is proposing expanded economic transition workshops for older adults at the community center. That is my curriculum target audience. (4) The community is under visible stress — nine protests, Tom Bradley laid off, Betty Kowalski visibly strained. This actually strengthens the case for AV literacy education: people need to understand what is happening to them and what skills they can still build. (5) The grant application outcome is still unknown — I submitted in tick 8, that is two months ago. I should be hearing something. (6) My in-person visit to the district coordinator last tick left a document and a note. Either she has read it or she has not. Either she will call or she will not. I give it one more week before I try a different channel through Mark.

response.inner_monologue: Two months of runway and no income — I know the number and I am not pretending it away. The curriculum is real, the referral is real, and Mark Thompson is out there telling a school board that the town needs people who can teach this transition. I built that curriculum. I showed up in person last tick and did not apologize for it. Now I have to keep moving on every front simultaneously because I cannot afford to wait for one door to open before I knock on the next one. Lisa Freeman is the door I have been ignoring. Dorothy Chen figured it out before I did, and she is seventy years old. That is embarrassing in the most useful possible way — it tells me I have been too focused on the school district and not enough on the places that actually move fast when the community needs something.
